mainTopic: Carrying on שבת when the object shifts from its planned position on the body, and when two people carry one object together.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous topic: the unusual carrying habit of the people of הוצל does not count against what everyone else does. A new משנה teaches that if someone planned to carry an object in front of him and it slid behind him, he is פטור, but if he planned behind and it slid to the front, he is חייב. A woman's סינר, and according to רבי יהודה couriers' notes, are חייב either way, because their position commonly shifts. רבא explains the difference: aiming for better protection and getting worse is not like aiming for worse and getting better. רבי אלעזר says the משנה comes from two different תנאים, because the רישא and the סיפא seem to imply opposite rulings for 'behind and stayed behind.' רב אשי answers that the משנה is a 'לא מיבעיא' build-up, so there is no contradiction. A ברייתא about coins in a money belt then shows that everyone agrees 'behind and stayed behind' is חייב. A second משנה teaches that two people who carry one loaf together are פטור unless neither could carry it alone, and רבי שמעון says פטור even then. The גמרא lays out the opinions of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון and derives the rule from the word 'בעשותה': only one who does the whole act is חייב.

steps.title: The unusual practice of one town does not count
steps.stepSummary: This closes the previous discussion. Even if the people of הוצל carry things in an unusual way, their habit is cancelled out by the normal behavior of everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say that the people of הוצל do it this way, their opinion is cancelled out by the practice of all other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier topic. One town's strange way of carrying does not make that kind of carrying a normal, punishable מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion ruled that carrying in an unusual manner (for example, on the head) is פטור. Someone might object that the people of הוצל really do carry this way. The answer is that what counts as normal carrying is set by most people, not by one place's custom. So 'בטלה דעתן' means their practice does not change the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of הוצל, a town whose residents had an unusual way of carrying
Their view is cancelled out and does not count
Compared with what all other people do

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic principle for שבת law: what counts as a normal way of doing a מלאכה is measured by the general population, not by one small group.

phrases.english: And if you want to say
that the people of Hotzal do so
phrases.notes: They carry in this unusual way.

phrases.english: their view is cancelled out compared to all other people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the sugya from the previous daf. This is the first step of this passage.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A minority custom does not turn an unusual way of carrying into a normal one. The practice of the majority decides.

steps.title: Planned in front but ended up behind, or the reverse
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules on two cases. If a person meant to carry in front and the object slid behind, he is פטור. If he meant to carry behind and it slid to the front, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who intends to carry an object out in front of him, and it ends up behind him, is exempt. If he intended behind him and it ended up in front of him, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens when the object moves to a different spot on the body than the person planned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases look like mirror images, but they get opposite rulings. Front-to-back is פטור. Back-to-front is חייב. The משנה gives no reason, and this unexplained difference is exactly what the גמרא will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
One who intends
To carry out from one domain to another
In front of him / behind him
Exempt / liable

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the two cases must get the same ruling just because they look like opposites. The משנה deliberately treats them differently, and the rest of this passage tries to explain why.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who intends to carry out [an object] in front of him,
and it came to be behind him, is exempt.
[If he intended] behind him and it came to be in front of him, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planned in front, ended up behind: פטור. Planned behind, ended up in front: חייב.

steps.title: A woman's apron and couriers' notes count either way
steps.stepSummary: A woman who carries something in her סינר is חייב whether it ends up in front or behind, because a סינר often turns around. רבי יהודה adds that couriers who carry notes are treated the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth they said: a woman who wears a סינר is liable whether the object was in front of her or behind her, because the סינר tends to turn around. רבי יהודה says: the same applies to those who receive notes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds special cases where it makes no difference whether the object ends up in front or behind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סינר commonly shifts around the body, so the woman expects her object might move. Ending up on the other side is therefore not a change from her plan, and she is חייב either way. רבי יהודה applies the same idea to couriers, who tuck notes into their belts without caring where they sit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In truth they said': a phrase that introduces an established, accepted law
Girds herself with a סינר, a garment worn tied around the body
It is likely to turn around
Those who receive notes, meaning couriers or messengers

phrases.english: In truth they said:
A woman who girds herself with a sinar,
whether in front of her or behind her, is liable,
since it is likely to turn around.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף מְקַבְּלֵי פִתְקִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Also those who receive notes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives special cases within the same משנה where the front-or-behind difference does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the object is expected to shift anyway (a סינר, or couriers' notes according to רבי יהודה), the person is חייב in either direction.

steps.title: Why should the two cases be treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why only front-to-back is פטור. In the back-to-front case the person's plan also did not happen, so he should be פטור too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about 'in front, and it ended up behind,' that he is exempt? Because his plan was not carried out. But in 'behind, and it ended up in front' as well, his plan was not carried out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It argues that both cases should have the same ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the reason for פטור is simple: what he did was not what he planned. If that is the reason, it applies equally to both directions. So the חייב ruling in the second case seems inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
His plan was carried out
Also

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about [intending] in front of him
and it came to be behind him, that he is exempt?
Because his intention was not carried out.
[In the case of] behind him and it came to be in front of him, also,
his intention was not carried out!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לְפָנָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of the משנה's first two rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's opposite rulings for front-to-back (פטור) and back-to-front (חייב).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for פטור is that the plan did not happen, that reason applies in both directions, so both cases should be פטור.

steps.title: The משנה comes from two different authors
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה is 'broken.' The two rulings come from two different תנאים who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is broken. The one who taught this ruling did not teach that ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר settles the contradiction by saying the two halves of the משנה do not come from the same author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not try to make the two rulings fit together. Instead, it says each ruling reflects a different תנא's opinion. The difference between the cases is a מחלוקת, not one consistent rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is broken: the משנה is not one unified statement

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: The one who taught this did not teach that, meaning two different תנאים

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: It is broken;

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: the one who taught this did not teach that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source: the two clauses come from two different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the whole משנה was one author with one consistent reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two rulings reflect a מחלוקת between two תנאים.

steps.title: Better protection versus worse protection explains the difference
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the question is not a real difficulty. Front-to-back is פטור because he aimed for better protection and got worse. Back-to-front is חייב because he aimed for worse protection and got better.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps 'in front, and it ended up behind' is exempt because he intended excellent protection and ended up with lesser protection. 'Behind, and it ended up in front' is liable because he intended lesser protection and ended up with excellent protection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the question of step 4. He shows that the two cases are not true mirror images, so there is no need to split the משנה for this reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in front is safer because you can see the object. If he wanted the safer way and got the weaker one, his plan was not fulfilled. If he settled for the weaker way and got the safer one, he got even more than he wanted, so his plan counts as carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (a phrase that rejects a question)
Perhaps
Excellent, superior protection
Lesser, weaker protection
What he ended up achieving

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a result which is better than intended still counts as fulfilling the intention. Only a worse result breaks the link between the plan and the act.

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps: [intending] in front of him and it came to be behind him,
this is the reason he is exempt:
because he intended excellent protection
and he ended up with lesser protection;
[intending] behind him and it came to be in front of him,
this is the reason he is liable:
because he intended lesser protection
and he ended up with excellent protection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the question of step 4, which makes רבי אלעזר's answer unnecessary for that question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question wrongly treated the two cases as equal. Getting less than you planned differs from getting more than you planned.

steps.title: The real problem: inferences from the two halves contradict
steps.stepSummary: רבא states the true difficulty. The רישא implies that 'behind and stayed behind' is חייב, while the סיפא implies that the same case is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the difficulty? The inference from the משנה is difficult. 'Intends in front, and it ended up behind: exempt' implies that 'behind and stayed behind' is liable. Look at the latter clause: 'behind, and it ended up in front' is the case that is liable, which implies that 'behind and stayed behind' is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a better question. Both halves of the משנה lead to opposite conclusions about the same middle case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the רישא: only a change from front to back makes him פטור, so carrying behind as planned should be חייב. From the סיפא: the משנה stresses that back-to-front is חייב, which suggests that plain behind-to-behind is פטור. The case where the object stays behind, exactly as planned, gets two opposite rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
An inference drawn from the exact wording
Read the latter clause
This implies (that the reverse case gets the opposite ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: The case in dispute here is not mentioned openly in the משנה. It is 'meant behind, and it stayed behind,' and we only reach it by inference from both halves.

phrases.english: Rather, what is the difficulty?
The inference from the mishna is difficult:
One who intends to carry out in front of him
and it came to be behind him is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: this implies: [intending] behind him and it came to be behind him, he is liable.
Read the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְפָנָיו הוּא דְּחַיָּיב,
phrases.english: [intending] behind him and it came to be in front of him is when he is liable;

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו פָּטוּר!
phrases.english: this implies: behind him and it came to be behind him, he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי קוּשְׁיָא — דִּיּוּקָא דְמַתְנִיתִין קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first question, רבא gives the real difficulty that justifies רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the רישא and the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא implies that behind-to-behind is חייב. The סיפא implies that behind-to-behind is פטור. These two inferences contradict each other.

steps.title: Two authors after all, now for the right reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's answer applies to this new question. The רישא and the סיפא come from two different תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is broken. The one who taught this ruling did not teach that ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי אלעזר's answer, now as the answer to the true contradiction from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two inferences cannot be reconciled, so the משנה must contain two opinions. One תנא holds that behind-to-behind is חייב, and the other holds that it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who said the משנה comes from two authors

steps.whatToRemember: The first question (why should the two cases differ?) is answered by רבא's protection logic. The real problem is the contradiction between the inferences from the רישא and the סיפא, and that is why רבי אלעזר says the משנה has two authors. The next step brings רב אשי, who rejects this contradiction and reads the משנה as one unified statement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: It is broken;

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: the one who taught this did not teach that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source between two תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One author wrote the entire משנה, so its inferences should agree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא and the סיפא reflect different תנאים, so the inferences about behind-to-behind may contradict each other.

steps.title: רב אשי: The משנה Is Teaching a Build-Up, So There Is No Contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says there is no real difficulty. The משנה uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style: of course 'behind and stayed behind' is חייב, and the משנה adds that even 'behind and came out in front' is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is the difficulty? Maybe the משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that if he meant to carry it behind him and it stayed behind him, he is חייב, because his plan happened. The משנה needed to teach that even if he meant behind and it came out in front, he is חייב. You might have thought: since his plan did not happen, he should not be חייב. So the משנה teaches us that if he aimed for weaker protection and ended up with better protection, he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רבא's difficulty from Step 7. He shows a way to read the משנה with no contradiction, so there is no need to split it between two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed the סיפא implies that 'behind and stayed behind' is פטור. רב אשי says the סיפא is simply skipping the obvious case and teaching the bigger new idea. The obvious case is 'behind and stayed behind,' which is חייב because his plan happened. The new idea is that 'behind but came out in front' is also חייב, because he got better protection than he planned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not necessary to say.' The obvious case is skipped so the text can teach a bigger new idea.
His plan (intention) was carried out.
'It would have entered your mind to say.' This introduces the mistaken first thought.
'It teaches us.' This introduces the actual new lesson.
Weaker protection / better protection of the object being carried.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is NOT saying that 'behind and stayed behind' is פטור. He is saying it is so obviously חייב that the משנה did not bother to state it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is saying 'it is not necessary':

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו דְּחַיָּיב —
phrases.english: It is not necessary to say that if he meant behind him and it came behind him, he is liable
because his intention was carried out,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְפָנָיו
phrases.english: but even if he meant behind him and it came in front of him
was necessary for it to teach.
It would have entered your mind to say,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְלָא אִיתְעֲבִידָא מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ לָא לִיחַיַּיב —
phrases.english: since his intention was not carried out, he should not be liable
so it teaches us
that since he intended weaker protection
and ended up with better protection, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי: מאי קושיא? דילמא לא מיבעיא קאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's difficulty from Step 7, which made רבי אלעזר's 'two תנאים' answer in Step 8 necessary.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the סיפא implies 'behind and stayed behind' is פטור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא read the סיפא's silence as a ruling. In fact, the סיפא is a 'לא מיבעיא' build-up that skips the obvious case.

steps.title: Claim: 'Behind and Stayed Behind' Is Debated by תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא claims that the case of 'intended behind, came out behind' is a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case of 'behind him and it came behind him' is a disagreement of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a short claim and sets up a proof for it in the next step. If the claim is true, it would fit רבי אלעזר's idea that different parts of the משנה come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי just said 'behind and stayed behind' is obviously חייב. This line suggests it is not so obvious, because some תנאים might say פטור. That would bring back the possibility of a 'broken' משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים (sages of the משנה era).

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו תַּנָּאֵי הִיא.
phrases.english: And 'behind him and it came behind him' is a dispute of tanna'im.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולאחריו ובא לו לאחריו תנאי היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's assumption that 'behind and stayed behind' is obviously חייב, and leans back toward רבי אלעזר's 'two תנאים' approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether 'intended behind, came behind' is חייב is debated by תנאים.

steps.title: The ברייתא of Coins in a Money Belt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: carrying coins in a belt with the opening up is חייב. With the opening down, רבי יהודה says חייב and חכמים say פטור. Each side brings an argument, and neither side could answer the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One who carries out coins in his money belt with its opening facing up is חייב. If the opening faces down, רבי יהודה says חייב and the חכמים say פטור. רבי יהודה said to them: Don't you agree that 'behind him and it came behind him' is חייב? They said to him: Don't you agree that carrying backhanded or with the foot is פטור? רבי יהודה said: I said one point and they said one point. I could not answer their point, and they could not answer mine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove the claim from Step 10. רבי יהודה's argument seems to show that 'behind and stayed behind' is part of the debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A belt with its opening down is an odd way to carry coins. רבי יהודה compares it to carrying behind oneself, which is also an odd but acceptable way, so he says חייב. The חכמים compare it to carrying backhanded, which is too unusual to count, so they say פטור. Neither side could refute the other.

keyTerms.meaning: His money belt, a hollow belt for holding coins.
Its opening facing up / its opening facing down.
In a backhanded (unusual) way. This kind of carrying is פטור on שבת.
'Don't you agree?' A debating challenge that points to a case the other side should accept.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One who carries out coins in his money belt
with its opening facing up is liable.
If its opening faces down,
Rabbi Yehuda holds him liable, and the Sages exempt him.
Rabbi Yehuda said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים בִּלְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו
phrases.english: Do you not agree regarding 'behind him and it came behind him'
that he is liable?
And they said to him: And do you not agree
regarding backhanded carrying or with his foot, that he is exempt?
Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי דָּבָר אֶחָד וְהֵן אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: I said one thing and they said one thing.
I did not find a response to their words
and they did not find a response to my words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source meant to prove the claim of Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That 'intended behind, came behind' is debated by תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the money belt and the exchange between רבי יהודה and the חכמים.

steps.title: The Inference: The חכמים Must Hold 'Behind' Is Exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asked 'Don't you agree?' This seems to show that the חכמים actually disagree and say 'behind and stayed behind' is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said to them 'Don't you agree,' doesn't that imply that the חכמים say פטור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly how the ברייתא proves the claim from Step 10. The wording 'Don't you agree' is read as a sign that the other side really disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים already agreed that 'behind and stayed behind' is חייב, there would seem to be no need to ask them 'Don't you agree.' So the גמרא infers that the חכמים hold it is פטור. That would make the case a real מחלוקת תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By implication.' Something is inferred from what was said.
The חכמים rule him exempt.

phrases.english: Since he said to them 'Do you not agree,'
is it not implied that the Rabbis exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: מדקאמר להו אי אתם מודין לאו מכלל דפטרי רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים hold 'behind and stayed behind' is פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'אי אתם מודין' in רבי יהודה's challenge.

steps.title: Challenge: By That Logic, רבי יהודה Would Hold Backhanded Carrying Liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the inference around. The חכמים also asked 'Don't you agree,' so by the same logic רבי יהודה would hold backhanded carrying חייב. But another ברייתא says everyone agrees backhanded carrying is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, since they said to him 'Don't you agree,' does that imply that רבי יהודה holds חייב? But it was taught: backhanded or with the foot, everyone agrees he is פטור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference from Step 12 by applying the same logic to the other side's words. This shows that the inference proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'Don't you agree' always means the other side disagrees, then רבי יהודה would hold backhanded carrying is חייב. But a ברייתא states clearly that everyone says פטור. So 'Don't you agree' must not imply disagreement. It just appeals to a case both sides accept.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning.' The same logic is turned against the one who used it.
'But wasn't it taught?' A ברייתא is brought to contradict a claim.
Everyone agrees.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
since they said to him 'Do you not agree,'
is it implied that Rabbi Yehuda holds liable?
But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר יָדוֹ וְרַגְלוֹ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּטוּר!
phrases.english: Backhanded or with his foot, everyone agrees he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וליטעמיך דקאמרי ליה אי אתה מודה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that 'Don't you agree' means the other side disagrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would force רבי יהודה to say backhanded carrying is חייב, which contradicts an explicit ברייתא saying everyone holds פטור.

steps.title: Correct Reading: Both Sides Agree on Both Cases and Argue Only About the Belt
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees 'behind and stayed behind' is חייב, and everyone agrees backhanded carrying is פטור. The only debate is which case the upside-down belt resembles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'behind him and it came behind him' — everyone agrees he is חייב. Backhanded or with the foot — everyone agrees he is פטור. Where they argue is the belt with its opening facing down. One Master compares it to 'behind him and it came behind him,' and the other Master compares it to backhanded or foot carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the ברייתא. This removes the claim from Step 10 that 'behind and stayed behind' is debated by תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'Don't you agree' questions point to cases that both sides already accept. The real debate is only about comparison. רבי יהודה says the downward-facing belt is like carrying behind oneself, so חייב. The חכמים say it is like backhanded carrying, so פטור. Since 'behind and stayed behind' is agreed by everyone to be חייב, רב אשי's reading of the משנה holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' This introduces the corrected reading.
'Where they disagree.' This identifies the exact point of the dispute.
'This Master compares it to.' Each side likens the case to a different known case.

steps.whatToRemember: (1) 'Intended behind, came behind' is חייב according to everyone. (2) Backhanded or foot carrying is פטור according to everyone. (3) The only debate is the money belt facing down: רבי יהודה compares it to carrying behind and says חייב, while the חכמים compare it to backhanded carrying and say פטור. (4) So רב אשי's 'לא מיבעיא' reading of the משנה stands.
steps.confusionAlert: In a debate, 'Don't you agree?' does not mean the other side disagrees. Each side is pointing to a case both already accept, to prove which case the disputed one resembles.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method of מחלוקת in the גמרא: both sides accept the same principles, and they argue only about which category a borderline case belongs to.

phrases.english: Rather:

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Behind him and it came behind him: everyone agrees he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר יָדוֹ וְרַגְלוֹ, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Backhanded or with his foot: everyone agrees he is exempt.
Where they disagree is his money belt with its opening down:

phrases.aramaic: מָר מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו,
phrases.english: One Master likens it to 'behind him and it came behind him,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְאַחַר יָדוֹ וְרַגְלוֹ.
phrases.english: and the other Master likens it to backhanded or foot carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא לאחריו ובא לו לאחריו דברי הכל חייב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from Step 13 by rereading the ברייתא, and cancels the claim of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא: both 'Don't you agree' questions refer to agreed-upon cases, and the dispute is only about comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Don't you agree' implied that the חכמים say 'behind and stayed behind' is פטור, making it a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone holds 'behind and stayed behind' is חייב and backhanded carrying is פטור. They argue only about whether the downward-facing belt resembles the first case or the second.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'Intended behind, came behind' is unanimously חייב, which supports רב אשי's 'לא מיבעיא' reading of the משנה.

steps.title: Whatever starts with 'In truth' is settled law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'באמת אמרו האשה' and cites a teaching that every 'באמת' in the משנה marks an accepted הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'In truth they said: a woman...' A teaching says: every time the משנה says 'In truth,' it is an accepted הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next phrase of the משנה, 'באמת אמרו', and explains what the word 'באמת' signals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'באמת' is a code word. It tells us the ruling is not a debated opinion but an accepted הלכה. So the case of the woman's סינר, where an object moved to the other side and she is חייב, is settled law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In truth.' A משנה opening that marks an accepted הלכה
'It was taught.' Introduces a teaching from the תנאים
'Etc.' The quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: 'In truth they said: a woman...' etc.
It was taught: every 'In truth' is an accepted law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the belt debate to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every 'באמת' in the משנה is an accepted הלכה.

steps.title: Even note-carriers are liable, because royal scribes carry that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's addition that even people who carry notes are חייב, and gives the reason: royal scribes carry notes this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even those who receive notes are liable. A teaching explains: this is because the king's scribes carry notes this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's line from the משנה and brings a teaching that explains why note-carriers are חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's addition follows the same logic as the סינר. Royal scribes tuck notes into their belts on every side, so a note's position, front or behind, does not matter to them. A note that ends up on the other side is therefore no change from the plan, and the courier is חייב either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who receive and pass on notes (couriers)
Royal scribes

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אַף מְקַבְּלֵי פִתְקִין.]
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: even those who receive notes.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: שֶׁכֵּן לַבְלָרֵי מַלְכוּת עוֹשִׂין כֵּן.
phrases.english: It was taught: because royal scribes do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: שֶׁכֵּן לַבְלָרֵי מַלְכוּת עוֹשִׂין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Note-carriers are חייב because carrying notes in a belt is the normal way for royal scribes.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the belt section. A way of carrying counts as normal, and so is חייב, if that is how people usually carry that item.

steps.title: New משנה: two people carrying one loaf
steps.stepSummary: One person who carries a loaf out is חייב. Two who carry it together are פטור. If one person could not carry it alone, the two are חייב, but רבי שמעון says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries a loaf out to the public domain is liable. If two carried it out, they are exempt. If one could not carry it alone and two carried it, they are liable. רבי שמעון exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: what happens when two people do one act of carrying together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that splitting a job between two people makes them פטור. The exception is when the job needs two people. Then working together is the normal way to do it, so they are חייב. רבי שמעון does not accept this exception.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
A loaf (of bread)
The public domain
Exempt (not liable)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the first case as 'two people always exempt.' The משנה goes on to say they are חייב when one person alone could not have done it, except according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who carries a loaf out to the public domain is liable.
If two carried it out, they are exempt.
If one could not carry it out alone
and two carried it out, they are liable.
And Rabbi Shimon exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא כִּכָּר לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people who share a carrying are פטור unless one alone could not do it. רבי שמעון says פטור even then.

steps.title: Three cases of two people doing one act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets out three cases. If both are able to do it alone, רבי מאיר says חייב while רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say פטור. If neither is able, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say חייב while רבי שמעון says פטור. If one is able and one is not, everyone says חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב (some say אביי said it, some say a ברייתא taught it): If each could do it alone, רבי מאיר says liable, and רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say exempt. If neither could do it alone, רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר say liable, and רבי שמעון says exempt. If one could and one could not, all agree he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא organizes the משנה's debate into a clear chart of three cases and shows who holds what in each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה's first, unnamed opinion matches רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר is the most strict: two people are always חייב. רבי שמעון is the most lenient: two people are always פטור. In the mixed case, the one who is able is really the one doing the work, and the weaker helper adds nothing, so the able one is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say it.' Gives another version of who said the teaching
Each one is able to do it alone
Holds liable
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The chart is: both able, only רבי מאיר says חייב. Neither able, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say חייב. One able and one not, everyone says חייב (the able one).

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say Abaye said it,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
If this one is able and that one is able,
Rabbi Meir holds them liable,
and Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon exempt.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל —
phrases.english: If this one is unable and that one is unable,
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir hold them liable,
and Rabbi Shimon exempts.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה יָכוֹל וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: If this one is able and that one is unable, all agree he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and expands the משנה's debate
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both able: רבי מאיר says חייב, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say פטור. Neither able: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say חייב, רבי שמעון says פטור. One able and one not: everyone says חייב.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the three-opinion chart
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא spells out the same three opinions: רבי מאיר says חייב, רבי יהודה makes it depend on ability, and רבי שמעון says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: One who carries a loaf out is liable. If two carried it out, רבי מאיר says liable. רבי יהודה says: if one could not carry it and two did, they are liable, and if not, they are exempt. רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that confirms the chart from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly names all three opinions. This proves that the unnamed opinion in our משנה is רבי יהודה, and that רבי מאיר holds two people חייב in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught so.' Introduces a supporting ברייתא
'And if not'

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
One who carries a loaf out to the public domain is liable.
If two carried it out, Rabbi Meir holds them liable,
and Rabbi Yehuda says:
If one could not carry it out alone
and two carried it out, they are liable,
and if not, they are exempt,
and Rabbi Shimon exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the chart in step 18
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא naming רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון

steps.title: Where do these rules come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of these rules about two people sharing one act.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules are now clear, but we need to know which verse teaches that people who share one act can be פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these words?' A request for a Torah source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the verse behind the rulings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind the exemption of two people who share one act

steps.title: The verse 'בעשותה': only one who does the whole act
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בעשותה' ('by doing it') teaches that only someone who does the entire act is חייב. Two people holding one tool together, whether gathering, weaving, writing, or carrying, are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'By doing it' means one who does all of it, not one who does part of it. How so? Two people were holding a pitchfork and gathering, a weaving tool and weaving, a pen and writing, or a reed and carrying it out to the public domain. You might think they are liable. So the verse says 'By doing it': one who does all of it, not one who does part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching from the רבנן that reads the word 'בעשותה' as requiring one person to do the whole act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about bringing a חטאת (sin-offering) says 'בעשותה', 'by doing it.' This means the person must do the act in full. When two people share one act, each did only part of it, so neither one is חייב. The examples show that this rule covers many מלאכות, not just carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By doing it.' The verse about bringing a חטאת
Part of it
A pitchfork for gathering stalks
A weaving tool used to beat the threads
'The verse teaches.' Introduces the Torah's answer

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that the one who does part of an act is פטור, is the basic principle behind every case where two people share a מלאכה on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: 'בעשותה' means you must do the whole act yourself. Splitting an act between two people that one person alone could do makes each of them פטור.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught: 'By doing it':
one who does all of it
and not one who does part of it.
How so?
Two who were holding a pitchfork and gathering,
a weaving tool and beating the threads,
a pen and writing,
a reed and carried it out to the public domain,
you might think they are liable.
So the verse says: 'By doing it':

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹשֶׂה אֶת כּוּלָּהּ וְלֹא הָעוֹשֶׂה מִקְצָתָהּ.
phrases.english: one who does all of it, and not one who does part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בעשותה' excludes someone who does only part of the act, such as two people sharing one act.
